stem:
The spontaneity (feasibility) of a chemical reaction depends on the standard Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G^{\circ}$. This is related to the standard enthalpy and entropy changes by the equation shown.

$$\Delta G^{\circ} = \Delta H^{\circ} - T\Delta S^{\circ}$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: State and explain whether the following processes will lead to an increase or decrease in entropy.
parts.text: the reaction of magnesium with hydrochloric acid

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: solid potassium chloride dissolving in water

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Magnesium carbonate can be decomposed.

$$\text{MgCO}_{3}\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{MgO}\text{(s)} + \text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H^{\circ} = +117\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Standard entropies are shown in the table.

| substance | $\text{MgCO}_{3}\text{(s)}$ | $\text{MgO}\text{(s)}$ | $\text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $S^{\circ}/\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$ | +65.7 | +26.9 | +214 |
parts.text:
Calculate $\Delta G^{\circ}$ for this reaction at $298\text{ K}$.
Include a relevant sign and give your answer to **three** significant figures.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to $\Delta G^{\circ}$, why this reaction becomes more feasible at higher temperatures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
On heating, sodium hydrogencarbonate decomposes into sodium carbonate as shown.

$$2\text{NaHCO}_{3}\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{Na}_{2}\text{CO}_{3}\text{(s)} + \text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O}\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H^{\circ} = +130\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta S^{\circ} = +316\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$$

Calculate the **minimum** temperature at which this reaction becomes spontaneous (feasible).
Show your working.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The solubility of Group 2 sulfates decreases down the Group.

Explain this trend.
